title: Skin boosters in Malaysia: Profhilo, Rejuran, Juvelook and exosomes explained
desc: What Profhilo, Rejuran, Juvelook and other skin boosters actually do, how many sessions they take, the risks, and how to check a clinic and product are legal.
headings: What are skin boosters? · How many sessions, and how long do results last? · Is it legal? What Malaysian rules say · How to check the doctor, clinic and product (the 3Ps) · Side effects and risks · Questions to ask at your consultation · How much do skin boosters cost?
keywords: Aesthetics & skin Skin boosters in Malaysia payudara kanser cancer mammogram pink october klinik doctor doktor gp aesthetic estetik kecantikan beauty kulit skin botox filler laser facial
body: “Skin booster” covers several different injectables: hyaluronic acid (such as Profhilo), polynucleotides (such as Rejuran) and collagen stimulators (such as Juvelook and Sculptra). These products are regulated as medical devices. Check that a product is on the Medical Device Authority (MDA) register. Only a registered doctor with a Letter of Credentialing and Privileging (LCP) may inject them, at an MOH-registered clinic. No exosome product appears on the MDA register, and cosmetics in Malaysia are for use on the skin only, not injection. Never have injections at homes, hotels or beauty salons. MOH calls this “checking the 3Ps”: procedure, practitioner and premises. “Skin booster” is a marketing term rather than a medical one. It usually means small amounts of an injectable placed just under the skin to improve hydration, texture, fine lines or firmness, rather than to add volume the way a lip or cheek filler does. The main types work quite differently: Type Examples How it works Hyaluronic acid (HA) Profhilo, Restylane Skinboosters, NCTF 135 HA Hyaluronic acid holds water in the skin, improving hydration and smoothness Polynucleotides (PN) Rejuran DNA fragments said to support skin repair; mostly studied in Korea Collagen stimulators Juvelook (PDLLA), Sculptra (PLLA) Microparticles trigger the skin to build collagen gradually over months Exosomes Various “exosome” serums Not registered as an injectable; see below Injectable treatments should only take place in an MOH-registered clinic. Hyaluronic acid boosters: in one study of Profhilo, women had two treatments four weeks apart, and improvement was still measurable at 16 weeks. Polynucleotides: a 2024 review found most studies used three to four sessions about two weeks apart. The authors noted the evidence is still limited and of low-to-moderate quality. Collagen stimulators: results build slowly. In the US trial for Sculptra, people had up to four sessions, and many still showed improvement two years later. Results vary between people, and most treatments need top-up sessions to maintain them. Be cautious of any promise of a fixed result or a fixed number of months. Skin booster injectables are regulated in Malaysia as medical devices . Products sold here must be registered with the Medical Device Authority (MDA). As of October 2026, the MDA register lists products including Profhilo, Rejuran, Sculptra, Restylane Skinboosters and NCTF 135 HA. You can search it yourself on the MDA medical device register . The Ministry of Health lists filler injections as a minimally invasive aesthetic procedure. They may only be done by a registered doctor holding a Letter of Credentialing and Privileging (LCP) , in premises registered under the Private Healthcare Facilities and Services Act 1998. A note on exosomes: searching the MDA register for “exosome” returns no products. In Malaysia, cosmetics are legally for use on the outside of the body, so a cosmetic exosome serum is not approved for injection. Doctors have reported cases of skin damage and scarring after exosome products meant for the skin were injected. The Ministry of Health urges the public to “check the 3Ps” before any aesthetic procedure: Practitioner: look the doctor up on the Malaysian Medical Council’s MeRITS register , and check MOH’s national registry of doctors with an LCP . Premises: the clinic should be registered with MOH. MOH publishes its list of registered private clinics, including those offering aesthetic services. Procedure and product: ask for the product’s name and check it on the MDA register. Make sure the procedure is one MOH allows. Breast and buttock fillers, for example, are illegal in Malaysia. Avoid injections at homes, hotels or salons In September 2026, raids in Shah Alam, Pandan Perdana and Kepong found unlicensed “therapists” offering aesthetic treatments in rented homes, promoted on TikTok and Instagram. Cheaper prices from unlicensed operators often mean unregistered products and no one to treat complications. Common, usually short-lived effects include bruising, redness, swelling, tenderness and small bumps at the injection points, which typically settle within days to a week. Less common but important risks: Lumps and nodules , particularly with collagen stimulators. In the Sculptra trial, 17% of patients developed nodules or bumps, sometimes appearing months later. Unlike hyaluronic acid, these cannot be dissolved with an enzyme. Injection into a blood vessel . This is rare but serious, and can cause skin damage, vision loss or stroke. It is the main reason injections should only be done by trained doctors who can recognise and treat it immediately. Infection and allergic reactions. Seek urgent medical care for severe or increasing pain, skin that turns pale, blue or dusky, or any change in your vision after an injection. Which product will you use, and is it registered with the MDA? Do you hold an LCP for this procedure? What results can I realistically expect, and how many sessions? What are the risks for me, and what happens if there is a complication? What is the total cost, including follow-up sessions? A careful doctor will review your medical history, medicines and allergies, explain alternatives, and give you time to decide. Be wary of pressure to book on the spot. Prices depend on the product, the amount used and the number of sessions. In October 2026, clinic adverts in Malaysia commonly listed skin booster treatments from around RM500 to over RM3,000 per session . Ask for a written quote that includes all planned sessions. A much lower price can be a warning sign of unregistered products or an unlicensed provider. Are skin boosters safe? When a registered product is injected by a trained, LCP-holding doctor in a registered clinic, side effects are usually mild and short-lived, such as bruising and swelling. Serious complications are rare but possible, which is why the doctor and clinic matter. Is exosome injection approved in Malaysia? No exosome product appears on the Medical Device Authority register, and cosmetics in Malaysia are legally for use on the skin, not injection. Ask your doctor exactly what product they plan to use and check its registration. How long do skin boosters last? It depends on the type. Hyaluronic acid boosters are usually repeated every few months, while collagen stimulators work gradually and can last longer. Most people need top-up sessions. Can a beautician do skin booster injections in Malaysia? No. Filler injections are a medical procedure in Malaysia. They may only be done by a registered doctor with a Letter of Credentialing and Privileging (LCP), in an MOH-registered clinic. How much is a skin booster in Malaysia? In October 2026, clinic adverts commonly listed skin boosters from around RM500 to over RM3,000 per session, depending on the product and number of sessions. Ask for a written quote.

title: Weight-loss injections in Malaysia: what Ozempic, Wegovy and Mounjaro can and can’t do
desc: Which injections are actually registered for weight loss in Malaysia, who they’re meant for, the side effects, and why “slimming pens” sold online are risky.
headings: What these injections are · Which ones are registered in Malaysia? · Who are they for? · How much weight do people lose? · Side effects and safety · Why “slimming pens” sold online are risky · What to expect when you see a doctor
keywords: Weight & metabolism Weight-loss injections in Malaysia Obesity Obesiti kencing manis gula hba1c darah tinggi hypertension bp tekanan darah mengandung hamil pregnancy antenatal klinik doctor doktor gp aesthetic estetik kecantikan beauty kulit skin botox filler laser facial
body: These medicines (GLP-1 medicines such as semaglutide, liraglutide and tirzepatide) are prescription-only in Malaysia. Only a registered doctor can prescribe them. Wegovy, Saxenda and Mounjaro are registered for weight management. Ozempic is registered for type 2 diabetes, not weight loss. They are meant for adults with a BMI of 30 or more, or 27 or more with a weight-related condition, alongside diet and exercise. Stomach side effects are common, and most people regain weight after stopping. Never buy “slimming pens” online or from salons. MOH has raided sellers and removed hundreds of listings in 2026. The injections people search for, such as Ozempic, Wegovy and Mounjaro, belong to a group of medicines that copy gut hormones called GLP-1 (and, for tirzepatide, also GIP). They make you feel full sooner, slow down how quickly the stomach empties, and help control blood sugar. Most are injected once a week with a pre-filled pen. In Malaysia they are Group B poisons under the Poisons Act 1952 . That means they can only be supplied by a registered doctor, or by a pharmacist with a doctor’s prescription. Selling them any other way is an offence. Every medicine sold legally in Malaysia carries a registration number starting with MAL , listed by the National Pharmaceutical Regulatory Agency (NPRA). As of October 2026, the register shows: Medicine (active ingredient) Registered in Malaysia for Wegovy (semaglutide 2.4 mg) Weight management Saxenda (liraglutide 3 mg) Weight management, including some teenagers aged 12+ Mounjaro (tirzepatide) Type 2 diabetes and, in the current product information, weight management Ozempic (semaglutide) Type 2 diabetes only, not weight loss Generic liraglutide Weight management (first generic registered in October 2026) Zepbound (tirzepatide) Not registered in Malaysia Registration can change, so you can always check a product yourself on the NPRA’s QUEST3+ product search . More than half of Malaysian adults (54.4%) are overweight or obese, according to the National Health and Morbidity Survey 2023. But these medicines are not meant for losing a few kilos before a holiday. The registered labels allow them for adults with: a body mass index (BMI) of 30 or more , or a BMI of 27 or more with at least one weight-related condition, such as prediabetes or type 2 diabetes, high blood pressure, high cholesterol, sleep apnoea or heart disease. Malaysia’s Clinical Practice Guidelines on obesity (2023) use lower BMI cut-offs for Asians when defining obesity (27.5 and above). They recommend medicines only alongside diet, physical activity and behaviour change, under a doctor’s supervision. A doctor will check your weight history, other conditions and medicines before suggesting any treatment. In the main clinical trials, adults taking semaglutide 2.4 mg lost about 15% of their body weight on average over 68 weeks, compared with about 2% on placebo. In the tirzepatide trial, average weight loss at the highest dose was about 21% over 72 weeks. Results vary a lot between people, and they depend on staying on treatment and keeping up healthy habits. The weight tends to come back after stopping. In one study, people regained about two-thirds of the weight they had lost within a year of stopping semaglutide. Many doctors therefore treat obesity as a long-term condition, like high blood pressure. Stomach and gut side effects are the most common, especially when starting or increasing the dose. In the semaglutide weight-management trials: Nausea: 44% (vs 16% on placebo) Diarrhoea: 30% Vomiting: 25% Constipation: 24% Less common but important risks include inflammation of the pancreas (pancreatitis), gallstones, hair loss and loss of muscle along with fat. They are not for use in pregnancy , and the product information advises stopping them before a planned pregnancy. People with a personal or family history of a rare thyroid cancer (medullary thyroid carcinoma) should not use semaglutide or tirzepatide. See a doctor urgently if you have Severe, persistent stomach pain, sometimes spreading to the back Repeated vomiting and signs of dehydration Yellowing of the skin or eyes In August 2026, the Ministry of Health warned the public about “pen kurus” sold online and claiming to contain retatrutide , an experimental medicine that is not approved anywhere in the world. Between January and July 2026, its Pharmacy Enforcement Division carried out 30 raids on weight-loss products, 17 of them involving online sales, and seized goods worth RM477,142. It also took down 209 e-commerce listings. Pens bought outside a clinic or pharmacy may be fake, unregistered, wrongly stored or the wrong dose. To protect yourself: Only get these medicines through a doctor who has assessed you. Check the box has a MAL registration number , and look it up on NPRA’s product search. Check the hologram security label (FarmaTag) with the FarmaChecker feature in the MyUBAT app. Avoid sellers on social media, e-commerce sites and in beauty salons. A doctor will usually ask about your weight history, eating habits, activity, sleep and other medicines. They will measure your weight, waist and blood pressure, and may arrange blood tests for blood sugar, cholesterol, and liver and kidney function. If a medicine is suitable, it is started at a low dose and increased slowly, with follow-up visits to check side effects and progress. A good weight-management plan also covers food, movement and sleep, and agrees what success looks like for you. For some people with a very high BMI, the doctor may discuss bariatric surgery. Is Ozempic approved for weight loss in Malaysia? No. In Malaysia, Ozempic is registered for type 2 diabetes. Wegovy, which contains a higher dose of the same medicine (semaglutide), is the version registered for weight management. Is Mounjaro available for weight loss in Malaysia? Mounjaro (tirzepatide) is registered in Malaysia, and its current product information includes weight management as well as type 2 diabetes. It is prescription-only, so a doctor must assess you first. Can I buy weight-loss injections online in Malaysia? You should not. These medicines are Group B poisons that need a prescription, and the Ministry of Health has raided sellers and removed online listings in 2026. Pens sold online may be fake or unregistered. Will I regain weight if I stop the injections? Many people do. Studies show a large part of the weight lost often returns within a year of stopping, which is why doctors pair medicines with long-term lifestyle changes.

title: Flu vaccine in Malaysia: who should get it, when, and how to get a free shot
desc: Flu circulates all year in Malaysia. Who should get vaccinated, the best timing, free shots for seniors, typical costs and what to expect.
headings: Why get a flu vaccine? · Who should get vaccinated · Free flu vaccines for seniors · When is the best time? · How much does it cost? · Which vaccine will I get? · Side effects and who should not have it
keywords: Prevention Flu vaccine in Malaysia Influenza Selesema kencing manis gula hba1c darah tinggi hypertension bp tekanan darah mengandung hamil pregnancy antenatal vaksin suntikan jab immunisation klinik doctor doktor gp
body: Flu circulates all year in Malaysia. The Ministry of Health advises a yearly vaccine, ideally in March or September. It is especially important for adults aged 60+, pregnant women, young children and anyone with a long-term illness. From 2026, free flu shots were reported to cover everyone aged 60+ and those aged 50–59 with a chronic illness. Book through MySejahtera. At private clinics, a flu shot is commonly advertised at roughly RM50–RM150. Side effects are usually mild, such as a sore arm or low fever for a day or two. Influenza is not just a bad cold. It can cause high fever, body aches and exhaustion that last a week or more. In older people, young children, pregnant women and people with heart, lung or kidney disease, it can lead to pneumonia and hospital stays. Flu circulates all year round in Malaysia, with surges. In late 2025, a wave of flu clusters swept through schools. By the end of October that year, flu-like illness still made up about 8% of clinic consultations, and severe respiratory infections about 10% of related hospital admissions. In September 2026, an influenza A cluster sickened dozens of students at a boarding school in Ipoh. Flu symptoms usually come on suddenly: fever, chills, aches, cough and tiredness. The Ministry of Health encourages a yearly flu vaccine, especially for: Adults aged 60 and over , particularly those with long-term heart, lung, kidney, liver or nerve conditions, or diabetes. Pregnant women , in any trimester. A vaccine in the third trimester also passes protection to the baby for the first months of life, according to Malaysia’s maternal immunisation guidelines. Children aged 6 months and older . Children under 9 having their first flu vaccine may need two doses a month apart, so ask your doctor. Anyone with a chronic illness , a weakened immune system, or who lives with someone at high risk. Healthcare and aged-care workers , and travellers and pilgrims . In 2025, the government offered free flu vaccines to people aged 60 and over with at least one chronic illness, at 649 selected government health clinics, booked through MySejahtera . In May 2026, news reports said the programme had widened. It now covers everyone aged 60 and over , and people aged 50–59 with at least one chronic condition such as diabetes, obesity, high blood pressure, high cholesterol, cancer, or heart, lung or kidney disease. You book a slot in MySejahtera at a Klinik Kesihatan, and walk-ins are accepted while stock lasts. Supply and dates can change during the year, so check MySejahtera or ask your nearest Klinik Kesihatan before you go. Because flu circulates all year here, any time is better than not at all. The Ministry of Health suggests March or September , ahead of the seasonal peaks. It takes about two weeks after the injection to build protection. If you are travelling to the northern hemisphere for the year-end holidays (Japan, Korea, China, Europe), where flu season runs roughly from November to January, get vaccinated at least two weeks before you fly. Haj and Umrah pilgrims should be vaccinated at least two weeks before arriving in Saudi Arabia. Check the current year’s requirements, as older pilgrims and high-risk groups have been required to have a flu vaccine. At private clinics and hospitals in Malaysia, a flu vaccine is commonly advertised at roughly RM50 to RM150 per dose, depending on the vaccine and whether a consultation is included. Ask the clinic for the full price before your appointment. Tax relief: vaccination costs for yourself, your spouse and your children can be claimed under the medical expenses tax relief, up to RM1,000 for vaccinations. From the 2026 year of assessment, this covers all vaccines registered with the NPRA, so keep your receipt. Flu viruses change every year, so the vaccine is updated every year to match the strains the World Health Organization expects to circulate. Since one influenza B strain (B/Yamagata) has not been detected anywhere since 2020, WHO now recommends three-strain (trivalent) vaccines. Malaysia has both trivalent and four-strain (quadrivalent) vaccines registered. Either protects against the strains currently circulating, and you do not need to choose a particular brand. Most people have no problems or mild, short-lived effects: A sore, red or swollen arm (very common) Low fever, headache, muscle aches or tiredness for a day or two Serious reactions are rare. The flu vaccine cannot give you flu , because the injected vaccine contains no live virus. It can be given on the same day as a COVID-19 vaccine. Do not have the vaccine if you have had a severe allergic reaction to a previous flu vaccine, and tell your doctor about any serious allergies. Babies under 6 months cannot be vaccinated. People with an egg allergy can usually still be vaccinated, so check with your doctor. If you have a high fever on the day, it is usually best to wait until you recover. Is the flu vaccine free in Malaysia? It can be if you are eligible. In 2026, free flu vaccines were reported to cover everyone aged 60 and over and people aged 50–59 with a chronic illness, booked through MySejahtera at government health clinics. Others can pay for a vaccine at a private clinic. How much is a flu vaccine at a private clinic in Malaysia? Private clinics and hospitals commonly advertise flu vaccines at roughly RM50 to RM150 per dose. Prices vary, so ask before your appointment. Vaccination costs can be claimed under the medical expenses tax relief. When is the best time to get a flu vaccine in Malaysia? The Ministry of Health suggests March or September. Flu circulates all year, so if you missed those months, get vaccinated now, and at least two weeks before any trip. Can I get the flu vaccine and a COVID-19 vaccine together? Yes. They can be given on the same day, usually in different arms. Can I get flu from the flu vaccine? No. The injected flu vaccine does not contain live virus. A sore arm or mild fever for a day or two is a normal response.

title: Haze is back in the Klang Valley: how to protect your family when the API climbs
desc: Every Selangor monitoring station read “unhealthy” this week. What the API means, which masks help, and how to protect children and older family members.
headings: What is happening now · What the API numbers mean · Who is most at risk · Simple ways to protect your family · Which masks actually help? · Heat is the next challenge · When to see a doctor
keywords: Prevention Haze and air quality Haze-related respiratory illness jerebu api ipu air pollutant index smoke kencing manis gula hba1c mengandung hamil pregnancy antenatal kecemasan emergency a&e hospital aesthetic estetik kecantikan beauty kulit skin botox filler laser facial
body: On 8 October 2026, all six Selangor monitoring stations recorded unhealthy air (API 101–200). Children, older people, pregnant women and anyone with asthma, COPD or heart disease are most at risk. Stay indoors with windows closed when the API is above 100, and use a well-fitted N95 mask if you must go out. See a doctor for wheezing, chest tightness or breathlessness that does not settle. For severe breathing difficulty, call 999. At 9am on 8 October 2026, 38 of Malaysia’s 68 air-quality monitoring stations recorded an unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) reading, between 101 and 200. Every station in Selangor was in that range: Johan Setia (178), Shah Alam (170), Banting (167), Klang (166), Petaling Jaya (165) and Kuala Selangor (155). In and around Kuala Lumpur, Putrajaya read 173, Cheras 172 and Batu Muda 168. The Department of Environment has linked the haze to fire hotspots across the Strait. On 29 September it reported 327 hotspots in Kalimantan and 191 in Sumatra. Johan Setia came close to “very unhealthy” on 18 September, reaching 198. The ASEAN weather centre expects haze to stay elevated from October to December 2026. Rain during the inter-monsoon period may bring some relief from late October, but conditions can change quickly from day to day. Check the latest reading for your area on the Department of Environment’s APIMS portal before planning time outdoors. API Status What to do 0–50 Good Normal activities. 51–100 Moderate Sensitive groups should watch for symptoms. 101–200 Unhealthy Cut down outdoor activity, especially for at-risk groups. Schools reportedly stop outdoor activities above 100. 201–300 Very unhealthy Stay indoors as much as possible. Selangor has said schools close at 200. Above 300 Hazardous Follow official instructions closely. Haze particles are small enough to reach deep into the lungs. Most healthy adults notice sore eyes, a scratchy throat or a cough. Some people are more likely to become unwell: Children , who breathe faster and spend more time active outdoors Older people , especially those with heart or lung disease Pregnant women Anyone with asthma, COPD, heart disease or diabetes The Ministry of Health has said it expects more asthma attacks and upper respiratory infections during the haze, and has advised high-risk groups to avoid outdoor activity, drink enough water and wear a mask if they have symptoms. Keep windows and doors closed when the API is above 100, and run the air-conditioner on recirculate. Use an air purifier with a HEPA filter in the room where you sleep, if you have one. Move exercise indoors or postpone it. Save your morning jog in the park for a clearer day. Drink plenty of water , which also helps with the heat. In the car , set the air-conditioning to recirculate. Keep medicines ready. If you have asthma, make sure your reliever inhaler is not expired and your action plan is up to date. On a clear day the view across Kuala Lumpur looks like this. Check the API before heading out. An N95 mask (or an equivalent such as KN95) filters fine haze particles much better than a surgical mask, as long as it fits snugly around the nose and chin. A surgical mask still helps with larger particles and is better than nothing. N95 masks may not fit young children properly, and some people with heart or lung disease find them hard to breathe through. For children, keeping them indoors on high-API days matters more than the mask. If you have a long-term heart or lung condition, ask your doctor before using an N95 for long periods. MetMalaysia has put the chance of a “Super El Niño” between October and December 2026 at more than 90%, with the hottest weather expected from February to May 2027. The Ministry of Health recorded 73 heat-related illnesses and 4 deaths nationwide between 1 January and 7 July 2026. Call 999 for possible heatstroke Very high body temperature with confusion, slurred speech or fainting Hot, dry skin, or a seizure Move the person somewhere cool, loosen clothing and cool them with water while waiting for help. See a GP if you have a cough, wheeze or sore throat that does not improve within a few days, if your asthma inhaler is needed more often than usual, or if a child seems unusually tired or breathless. Go to an emergency department or call 999 for severe shortness of breath, chest pain, blue lips or confusion. Is it safe to exercise outdoors during haze? When the API is above 100, it is better to exercise indoors or postpone. People with asthma, heart disease or other risk factors should avoid outdoor exertion altogether until air quality improves. Is a surgical mask enough for haze? A surgical mask blocks larger particles but lets many fine haze particles through. A well-fitted N95 or KN95 mask gives much better protection for adults. Where can I check the API for my area? The Department of Environment publishes live readings on its APIMS portal at eqms.doe.gov.my, updated every hour.

title: Dengue in the Klang Valley: what to watch for in the first three days
desc: Cases are up sharply in Selangor and KL this year. Warning signs, why rest and fluids matter, which painkillers to avoid, and when to go straight to A&E.
headings: Why 2026 has been a hard dengue year · What dengue is · The first three days · Warning signs · Caring for yourself at home · Prevention at home
keywords: Prevention Dengue in the Klang Valley Dengue fever Demam denggi denggi aedes nyamuk mosquito vaksin suntikan jab immunisation kecemasan emergency a&e hospital klinik doctor doktor gp aesthetic estetik kecantikan beauty kulit skin botox filler laser facial
body: Malaysia recorded 65,979 dengue cases by early September 2026, up 66% on the same period last year. Selangor has the most cases of any state. Dengue usually starts with a sudden high fever, headache and body aches. The riskiest time is often when the fever starts to come down , around days 3 to 7. Use paracetamol for fever. Avoid aspirin, ibuprofen and other NSAIDs. See a doctor for a blood test if a fever lasts more than two days. By epidemiological week 35, Malaysia had recorded 65,979 dengue cases and 62 deaths , up from 39,616 cases and 32 deaths over the same period in 2025. The Klang Valley has been hit hardest. By mid-August, Selangor had 25,090 cases (up 61%), while Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya together had 10,316 (up 106%). By 7 October, Selangor’s total for the year had passed 31,000, according to the iDengue portal. The Ministry of Health has linked the rise to a shift in the dominant virus type from DENV-2 to DENV-3 , a strain many people have little immunity to, along with erratic weather that alternates heavy rain and heat. More than 70% of mosquito breeding sites found by health officers are in and around homes. Dengue is a viral infection spread by Aedes mosquitoes, which bite mostly during the day. In a dense, humid region like the Klang Valley, they breed easily in small pockets of clean standing water: flower-pot trays, roof gutters, discarded containers. Many infections are mild. But a small number of people develop severe dengue, which needs hospital care. Knowing what to watch for helps you act at the right time. Symptoms usually appear 4 to 10 days after a mosquito bite. Common early signs include: Sudden high fever Severe headache and pain behind the eyes Muscle and joint pain Nausea, vomiting or loss of appetite A rash, sometimes appearing a few days in If a fever lasts more than two days, especially if someone nearby has had dengue, see a GP. A simple blood test (full blood count) helps your doctor track your platelets and hydration. Your doctor may ask you to return for repeat blood tests over several days. The critical phase often begins as the fever drops. Feeling a little better is not always a sign you are through it. Go to A&E or call 999 if you notice: Severe stomach pain or persistent vomiting Bleeding gums or nose, or blood in vomit or stools Fast breathing, or feeling very tired or restless Cold, clammy skin, or passing much less urine If your doctor says you can recover at home: Rest as much as you can, and take time off work or school. Drink often : water, oral rehydration salts, clear soups or coconut water. Use paracetamol for fever and pain, at the dose on the label. Avoid aspirin, ibuprofen and other NSAIDs , which can raise the risk of bleeding. Keep follow-up appointments , even if you feel better. Ten minutes a week makes a real difference. Walk around your home and empty, scrub or cover anything that holds water: plant trays, pails, pet bowls, roof gutters and air-conditioner drip trays. Use repellent during the day, and wear long sleeves outdoors in the early morning and late afternoon. Wolbachia mosquitoes: in some areas, health authorities release mosquitoes carrying Wolbachia bacteria, which reduce the spread of dengue. Officials credited the programme with a 36% drop in Putrajaya’s cases in early 2026. Vaccine: the Qdenga dengue vaccine received conditional approval in Malaysia in 2024 for people aged 4 and over, given as two doses three months apart. It is available at private clinics and hospitals but is not part of the national immunisation programme. Ask your doctor whether it suits you. Can I take ibuprofen if I think I have dengue? No. Use paracetamol for fever and pain. Ibuprofen, aspirin and other NSAIDs can increase the risk of bleeding in dengue. Is there a dengue vaccine in Malaysia? Yes. Qdenga has conditional approval for people aged 4 and over and is available privately. It is not part of the national immunisation programme, so ask your doctor whether it is suitable for you. How long after a mosquito bite do dengue symptoms start? Usually 4 to 10 days after the bite.

title: When should Malaysian women start breast screening?
desc: Half of breast cancers in Malaysia are found late. A gentle walkthrough of self-checks, clinical exams and mammograms, and how to get one free or subsidised.
headings: Why early detection matters in Malaysia · Know your normal · Clinical exams and mammograms: who and how often · Free and subsidised mammograms · What happens at a mammogram
keywords: Women's health Breast cancer screening Breast cancer Kanser payudara payudara kanser cancer mammogram pink october klinik doctor doktor gp saringan check-up checkup medical aesthetic estetik kecantikan beauty kulit skin botox filler laser facial
body: In 2017–2021, 50.5% of breast cancers in Malaysia were diagnosed at stage 3 or 4. Get to know how your breasts normally look and feel, and see a doctor about any change. Women aged 40–70 may qualify for a free LPPKN mammogram, depending on household income. PERKESO’s 2026 screening for contributors aged 40–59 includes a mammogram for women. Breast cancer is the most common cancer among Malaysian women. The Malaysia National Cancer Registry recorded 29,534 cases between 2017 and 2021, about a third of all cancers in women. Worryingly, 50.5% were found at stage 3 or 4 , up from 47.9% in 2012–2016. The National Cancer Society Malaysia (NCSM) estimates that fewer than 30% of eligible women have regular mammograms, and about half of breast cancers here are diagnosed before age 50. Cancers found early are far easier to treat, which is why Pink October focuses on screening. “Breast awareness” simply means knowing how your breasts usually look and feel, so you notice changes. Many women check once a month, a few days after their period ends. See a doctor if you notice: A new lump or thickening in the breast or armpit A change in size or shape Dimpling or puckering of the skin A nipple that turns inwards, or discharge (especially if bloody) A rash or redness around the nipple Pain in one area that does not go away Most lumps are not cancer. But only a doctor can tell, so it is always worth getting checked. A clinical breast examination is a check by a doctor or trained nurse, and is a good starting point at any age. A mammogram is a low-dose X-ray that can find cancers too small to feel. According to NCSM, the Ministry of Health’s 2022 recommendation is a mammogram every two years for women aged 50 to 74, and a discussion with a doctor about personal risk for women aged 40 to 49. If you have a strong family history of breast or ovarian cancer, talk to your doctor about starting earlier. A mammogram takes about 20 minutes. The squeeze is brief and usually more uncomfortable than painful. Programme Who it is for How to apply LPPKN mammogram programme Women aged 40–70. Free for household income of RM10,000 or less, RM50 subsidy above that. Women aged 35–39 with a family history may qualify with a doctor’s referral. Apply at mamogram.lppkn.gov.my or through Klinik Nur Sejahtera PERKESO health screening 2026 Active PERKESO (SOCSO) contributors aged 40–59. Includes a mammogram and Pap smear for women. Book through the SEHATi app Selangor Saring Selangor’s free state screening programme, which includes mammograms. Register through the SELangkah app Several private hospitals in the Klang Valley also run Pink October mammogram promotions until the end of October or November. Eligibility and availability change, so check the latest details before booking. You will undress from the waist up and stand in front of the machine. Each breast is gently pressed between two plates for a few seconds while the X-ray is taken. Avoid deodorant or talcum powder on the day, as it can show up on the image. Results usually go to the doctor who referred you, who will explain them and arrange any follow-up. At what age should I start having mammograms in Malaysia? NCSM reports that the Ministry of Health recommends a mammogram every two years from 50 to 74, with women aged 40–49 discussing their own risk with a doctor. Women with a strong family history may start earlier. Can I get a free mammogram in Selangor or Kuala Lumpur? Yes, if you are eligible. LPPKN offers free mammograms for women aged 40–70 with household income of RM10,000 or less, PERKESO screening includes mammograms for contributors aged 40–59, and Selangor Saring offers free screening for Selangor residents. Does a lump always mean cancer? No. Most breast lumps are not cancer, but every new lump should be checked by a doctor.

title: World Mental Health Day 2026: how to check in, and where to call in Malaysia
desc: Calls to Talian HEAL 15555 have more than tripled since 2023. Simple ways to check in on yourself and others, plus the helplines worth saving.
headings: This year’s theme · More Malaysians are reaching out · How to check in on someone · Looking after yourself · Helplines worth saving · How a GP can help
keywords: Mental wellbeing World Mental Health Day 2026 Mental health jerebu api ipu air pollutant index smoke kesihatan mental depression anxiety stress kemurungan kecemasan emergency a&e hospital klinik doctor doktor gp aesthetic estetik kecantikan beauty kulit skin botox filler laser facial
body: Talian HEAL 15555 received 90,981 calls in 2025, more than three times the 2023 total. About 1 million Malaysians aged 15 and over live with depression (NHMS 2023). Asking someone “How are you, really?” and listening without judging is a powerful first step. If someone is in immediate danger, call 999. The World Federation for Mental Health has chosen “Lived Experiences Heard: Real Voices, Real Change” as the theme for World Mental Health Day 2026. It is a reminder that people who have lived with mental health conditions have a great deal to teach the rest of us about what helps. The Ministry of Health’s free psychosocial support line, Talian HEAL 15555 , answered 27,738 calls in 2023, 42,990 in 2024 and 90,981 in 2025. By mid-June 2026 it had already taken 66,442 calls, and more than 230,000 since it launched in October 2022. Most callers are aged 18 to 35. The national picture shows why. The National Health and Morbidity Survey 2023 estimated that about 1 million people aged 15 and over have depression, double the 2019 figure, with the highest rate among those aged 16 to 19. Mental health problems among children aged 5 to 15 rose from 7.9% to 16.5%. There are also signs of progress. Attempted suicide is no longer a criminal offence in Malaysia since 2025, removing a barrier that kept some people from seeking help. The Ministry of Health runs 39 MENTARI community mental health centres, and in September 2026 it launched guidelines on supporting families and communities after a suicide. Pick a quiet moment : a walk, a drive, a teh tarik. Ask directly and kindly : “You’ve seemed a bit down lately. How are you, really?” Listen more than you talk. You do not need to fix anything. Do not judge or rush to advice. “That sounds really hard” goes a long way. Encourage support : a trusted person, a helpline, or a doctor. Offer to help make the call. Follow up a few days later. If you are worried that someone might harm themselves, it is okay to ask about suicide directly. Asking does not put the idea in their head, and it can be a relief to be asked. Small, steady habits help: regular sleep, daylight and movement, time with people who make you feel safe, and breaks from the news and your phone. Try a short breathing practice: breathe in for four counts, hold for four, breathe out for six, and repeat for a few minutes. Even a 10-minute walk outdoors can lift your mood. On haze days, walk indoors instead. Service Contact Hours Talian HEAL (Ministry of Health) 15555 8am to midnight daily Befrienders Kuala Lumpur 03-7627 2929 24 hours Talian Kasih 15999 or WhatsApp 019-261 5999 24 hours Emergency 999 24 hours Your family doctor is a good place to start. A GP can talk through how you are feeling, screen for depression and anxiety, check for physical causes such as thyroid problems, start treatment, and refer you to a psychologist, psychiatrist or a MENTARI centre if needed. Several clinics in our directory list mental health counselling among their services. What is Talian HEAL 15555? It is the Ministry of Health’s free psychosocial support line, open from 8am to midnight every day, including public holidays. Is there a 24-hour emotional support line in Kuala Lumpur? Befrienders Kuala Lumpur offers confidential emotional support 24 hours a day on 03-7627 2929. Can I see a GP for anxiety or depression? Yes. GPs can assess your symptoms, start treatment and refer you to specialist mental health services if needed.

title: Most young Malaysians with diabetes or high blood pressure don’t know it
desc: Over 80% of adults aged 18–29 with diabetes or high blood pressure are undiagnosed. Which simple checks you need, and how to get them free.
headings: What the new figures show · The bigger picture · Why it goes unnoticed · Three simple checks · How to get screened for free · Small habits that help
keywords: Heart & diabetes Undiagnosed diabetes & high blood pressure Type 2 diabetes Diabetes kencing manis gula hba1c darah tinggi hypertension bp tekanan darah payudara kanser cancer mammogram pink october mengandung hamil pregnancy antenatal klinik doctor doktor gp saringan check-up checkup medical
body: Over 80% of adults aged 18–29 with diabetes or high blood pressure are undiagnosed (NHMS 2023, cited in Parliament on 6 October 2026). Nationally, 15.6% of adults have diabetes and 29.2% have high blood pressure. A blood pressure reading, a blood sugar test and a cholesterol test can pick up most problems early. PERKESO contributors aged 40–59 can get free screening through the SEHATi app. On 6 October 2026, the Health Minister told Parliament that, according to the National Health and Morbidity Survey (NHMS) 2023, more than 80% of adults aged 18 to 29 who have diabetes or high blood pressure do not know it. That is about 192,000 young adults with diabetes and 340,000 with hypertension. The picture is only slightly better among people in their 30s: around 60% of those with diabetes and over 70% of those with hypertension are undiagnosed. Diabetes is also showing up earlier. By June 2026, 660 new cases had been registered among people under 30, after 1,932 in the whole of 2025. Condition (adults, NHMS 2023) Prevalence Undiagnosed Diabetes 15.6% (about 3.6 million) 5.9% of adults High blood pressure 29.2% (about 6.7 million) 11.9% of adults High cholesterol 33.3% (about 7.5 million) 18.1% of adults Overweight or obese 54.4% – Left unchecked for years, these conditions quietly raise the risk of heart attack, stroke, kidney disease and eye problems. Ischaemic heart disease alone caused 17,421 deaths in Malaysia in 2024. High blood pressure and early type 2 diabetes usually cause no symptoms at all . When symptoms do appear (thirst, passing more urine, tiredness, blurred vision, slow-healing wounds), the condition has often been there for some time. You may be at higher risk if you: Are overweight, especially around the waist Have a parent or sibling with diabetes or high blood pressure Had diabetes in pregnancy Smoke, sleep poorly, or sit for most of the day Drink sweet drinks most days Blood pressure : takes two minutes at any clinic or pharmacy. You can also check it at home . Blood sugar : an HbA1c or fasting glucose blood test. Cholesterol : a lipid profile blood test, often done at the same time. Your doctor will also look at your weight and waist size. If your results are borderline, small changes now can keep them from rising. PERKESO Health Screening Programme 2026 : for Malaysians aged 40–59 who are active contributors (at least 12 months of contributions). Book through the SEHATi app. It covers blood count, HbA1c, lipid profile, urine test, a physical exam and a doctor consultation, plus a Pap smear and mammogram for women. PeKa B40 : free health screening for eligible lower-income Malaysians aged 40 and over. Klinik kesihatan : government health clinics offer blood pressure and blood sugar checks at low cost. Under 40 and not eligible? A basic check at a private GP clinic is still quick and affordable, and well worth doing. Order kurang manis or kosong , and swap one sweet drink a day for plain water. Walk for 30 minutes on most days. Two 15-minute walks count too. Add more ulam and vegetables to your plate. Aim for seven hours of sleep. If you smoke, ask your doctor about help to quit. How do I know if I have high blood pressure? The only way to know is to measure it. Most people with high blood pressure feel completely well. Who can get PERKESO’s free health screening? Malaysians aged 40–59 who are active PERKESO contributors with at least 12 months of contributions. Book through the SEHATi app and check the latest eligibility there. Which blood test checks for diabetes? Usually an HbA1c test, which reflects your average blood sugar over the past two to three months, or a fasting blood glucose test.

title: A five-minute routine for checking blood pressure at home
desc: How to sit, when to measure, and what numbers to bring to your doctor, following Malaysia’s clinical guidelines.
headings: Why measure at home? · Choosing a monitor · The five-minute routine · What the numbers mean · Bringing readings to your doctor
keywords: Heart & diabetes Checking blood pressure at home Hypertension Darah tinggi darah tinggi hypertension bp tekanan darah kecemasan emergency a&e hospital klinik doctor doktor gp aesthetic estetik kecantikan beauty kulit skin botox filler laser facial
body: Use a validated, automatic upper-arm monitor with the right cuff size. Sit quietly with your back and arm supported for a few minutes before measuring. Take two readings, one minute apart, every morning and evening for up to seven days. Malaysian guidelines treat an average home reading above 135/85 mmHg as elevated. Blood pressure changes through the day, and some people read higher at the clinic simply because they are anxious (“white-coat” hypertension). Others read normal at the clinic but high at home. Malaysia’s Clinical Practice Guidelines on hypertension encourage home monitoring because it helps with diagnosis, empowers patients and can improve how well treatment works. Upper-arm, automatic. Wrist and finger monitors are less reliable. Validated for accuracy. Ask your pharmacist for a clinically validated model. The right cuff size. A cuff that is too small gives falsely high readings. Measure around your upper arm and check the range printed on the cuff. Memory function is handy, so you do not have to write every reading down. Prepare. No smoking, eating, caffeine or exercise for 30 minutes beforehand. Empty your bladder. Sit well. Back supported, feet flat, legs uncrossed, arm resting on a table so the cuff is at heart level. Rest quietly for a few minutes. No talking or scrolling. Measure twice , at least one minute apart, on bare skin. Record both readings straight away, with the date and time. Measure at about the same time in the morning (before medicines, if you take them) and in the evening (before dinner), for at least three days and ideally seven. Keep a simple logbook, or use a monitor that stores readings. Ignore the readings from the first day, then average the rest. According to Malaysia’s Clinical Practice Guidelines (Management of Hypertension, 5th edition), an average home reading above 135/85 mmHg should be considered elevated. Bring your logbook to your doctor, who will interpret it together with your clinic readings. Get help quickly See a doctor the same day if readings are repeatedly 180/110 mmHg or higher. Call 999 if a high reading comes with chest pain, breathlessness, weakness on one side, slurred speech or a sudden severe headache. Take your logbook or monitor to your next appointment. If you are on treatment, home readings help your doctor adjust your medicines safely. If you have never been diagnosed but your average is high, book a check-up. High blood pressure is very treatable, and lifestyle changes alone often help in the early stages. What is a normal home blood pressure reading? Malaysia’s hypertension guidelines treat an average home reading above 135/85 mmHg as elevated. Your doctor will advise on your personal target. Are wrist blood pressure monitors accurate? Upper-arm monitors are generally more reliable. If you use a wrist monitor, keep your wrist at heart level and check it against a clinic reading. Should I measure before or after taking my medicine? Measure in the morning before taking your blood pressure medicine, and in the evening before dinner.

title: Clinic or emergency department? A simple guide for Klang Valley families
desc: When to call 999, when to head to the emergency department, and when your neighbourhood GP is the better choice.
headings: Call 999 straight away for · Go to the emergency department for · See a GP for · Klinik kesihatan or private GP? · What to bring
keywords: Guides Clinic or emergency department? denggi aedes nyamuk mosquito kencing manis gula hba1c darah tinggi hypertension bp tekanan darah kesihatan mental depression anxiety stress kemurungan mengandung hamil pregnancy antenatal vaksin suntikan jab immunisation kecemasan emergency a&e hospital klinik doctor doktor gp saringan check-up checkup medical
body: Call 999 (or 112 from a mobile) for life-threatening emergencies. Go to an emergency department for urgent problems that cannot wait, such as dengue warning signs. For most fevers, coughs, minor injuries and ongoing conditions, a GP clinic is faster and better suited. Chest pain or pressure, especially spreading to the arm, jaw or back Signs of stroke: face drooping, arm weakness, slurred speech. Note the time symptoms started. Severe difficulty breathing, or blue lips Unconsciousness, a seizure, or sudden confusion Heavy bleeding that will not stop A severe allergic reaction with swelling of the face or throat Serious injury, such as after a road accident or a fall from height From a mobile phone you can also dial 112 . Dengue warning signs: severe stomach pain, persistent vomiting, bleeding, or drowsiness (see our dengue guide ) A fever of 38°C or higher in a baby under three months old Severe abdominal pain Suspected broken bones, deep cuts or burns Dehydration in a child who is not passing urine Heavy bleeding or severe pain in pregnancy Malaysian emergency departments use a triage colour system (red, yellow, green). The most urgent patients are seen first, so less urgent cases may wait longer. That is one reason a GP is often quicker for non-urgent problems. Most fevers, coughs, colds and sore throats A fever lasting more than two days (for a dengue blood test) Minor cuts, sprains and wound dressing Rashes, ear pain, urinary symptoms Diabetes, blood pressure and cholesterol follow-up Health screening, vaccinations, and medical certificates Mental health concerns, when there is no immediate danger A GP can treat most everyday illnesses and refer you to a hospital if needed. Government health clinics ( klinik kesihatan ) offer low-cost care, especially for long-term conditions, antenatal care and child vaccinations, but they usually keep office hours. Private GP clinics often open into the evening and on weekends, which helps when illness strikes after work. Many accept company panels or insurance, so bring your panel card. MyKad, MyKid or passport A list of medicines you take (or the boxes) Panel or insurance card For children: their health record book For pregnancy: your antenatal record book What is the emergency number in Malaysia? Dial 999 from any phone. From a mobile phone you can also dial 112. Should I go to a clinic or the emergency department for a high fever? For most adults and older children, a GP clinic is the right first stop. Go to the emergency department for a baby under three months with a fever of 38°C or more, or for dengue warning signs such as severe stomach pain, bleeding or persistent vomiting.
